title: Terminal login and personal comm-device (phone): a shared, self-uncovering information ecosystem
summary: Players log into the landing page with a password; on success it boots like a command-line terminal into either the campaign map or the player's personal terminal. That terminal grew into a full always-on-screen 'phone': an in-universe intranet browser mixing red herrings with genuinely critical info, searchable, hacking-skill-gated for more, with an automatic mass-mailing broadcast so a document one player uncovers becomes available to the whole table, organized for later lookup. Two audio assets (password required / user authenticated) already made.
description:
To make the interface feel 'real': the players' landing page requires a password to log in. Once authenticated, it updates to show real landing-page information, loading as if it were a computer booting at a command line, then opening to either the campaign map or the individual player's personal terminal. Broader idea attached: build an in-fiction information-serving system, accessible through a locally-available terminal or a personal device terminal, either of which gives players access to certain information by default — with a hacking mechanic layered on top, so a successful skill roll reveals additional information beyond the terminal's baseline access. This connects directly to the SF2E-terminology-reflavor idea's automated-Recall-Knowledge concept (both are about controlling exactly what information reaches players and when).

Two real audio assets already exist for this specific flow: a 'password required' sound and a 'user authenticated' sound.

**Grown substantially in a later message, as the third of three named in-scene UI elements** (alongside in-scene-ui-panel-mimetic-controls's control bar and in-scene-character-portrait-frames): this is the players' **personal communication device — always on screen**, not just a one-time login gate. Framed explicitly as 'a whole phone worth of contents' and 'a whole avenue of content': a browsable in-universe intranet/web mixing 'tons of fun and silly side things,' deliberate red herrings and diversions, and genuinely critical information — searchable, so a smart player piecing things together through search alone is a valid way to get ahead. The hacking skill is a direct-benefit tool here, not flavor: a successful hacking check pulls things out of the phone/intranet that plain browsing wouldn't surface.

**Art direction, now locked, with an explicit split between hardware and software**: the phone's **OS and on-screen visuals** are deliberately blocky, chunky, low-res/pixelated — not a slick modern smartphone UI. The **physical device itself** is allowed to be somewhat smoother and better-rendered, but still reads 1960s / retrofuturistic — think period industrial-design object housing a crude pixel display, not a modern phone and not a uniformly pixel-art sprite. Chosen partly for tone and explicitly partly for production practicality: chunky pixel art is easier to actually generate well than photorealistic or clean-vector UI. Needs real graphics, sound effects, and small cute animations for this to land — 'bonus points for cute' on the phone specifically, more than the other in-scene UI elements. The phone is **draggable — players can move it around the screen**, so it's a floating windowed element rather than a fixed dock like the control bar.

**New concrete mechanic: automatic mass-mailing on discovery.** When a player uncovers a piece of useful information through this system — text or image, any in-fiction document — the system automatically pings every player and grants them access to it too, rather than leaving it siloed with whoever found it first. Discovered material accumulates in 'a carefully organised form so that it's easy for people to look back through lore dump documents' — this is a real storage/browsability requirement, not just a one-time reveal, and overlaps with chat-log-knowledge-base and player-and-gm-journals-context-ingestion's shared goal of durable, queryable session content. Distinct from automated-recall-knowledge-system: that idea is specifically per-enemy Recall Knowledge reveals; this is the general case covering any discoverable in-fiction document.
sourceContext: User planning message, 2026-08-22 — large worldbuilding/tooling brain-dump. Substantially elaborated in a later planning message the same day, part of a multi-part rant about in-scene UI.
openSubQuestions: What information the baseline terminal exposes vs. what's gated behind a hacking roll.
Whether 'personal terminal' content differs meaningfully per player/kid.
Technical implementation — likely ties into whichever UI framework ends up handling the landing page and director's-panel-adjacent work.

Data model for 'a discovered document' (text vs. image, one schema for both?) and how the mass-mailing broadcast is actually implemented (a Foundry permission grant, a journal-visibility flip, a notification pointing at existing content?).
How red-herring volume gets balanced against critical info so browsing the phone stays fun rather than becoming a real-time sink during limited session time — not addressed yet.
